statement: Mainstream current Egyptology classifies Egyptian hieroglyphic writing as INDEPENDENT: "the earliest solid evidence of Egyptian writing differs in structure and style from the Mesopotamian and must therefore have developed independently." A stimulus-diffusion minority position (general awareness that writing was possible reaching Egypt via contact, not sign-borrowing) rests on real evidence of Egypt-Mesopotamia contact in the same period (Mesopotamian-style cylinder seals appear in Egyptian tombs from Naqada IIb-c, c. 3500-3300 BCE), but no serious current scholar argues hieroglyphs directly copied/modified cuneiform signs — the sign systems are structurally and visually too dissimilar for ADAPTATION.
scholarly_disagreement: INDEPENDENT (mainstream) vs. STIMULUS_DIFFUSION (documented minority position) — not INDEPENDENT vs. ADAPTATION, which is excluded by both camps.

interpretations.strongest_case: Regulski: proposed Sumerian/Elamite pictogram parallels to Predynastic Egyptian seals "cannot be proved" to show a proper writing system existed at that point comparable to the U-j labels — the seal-contact evidence establishes technology transfer, not sign-system transmission.

interpretations.position: General stimulus diffusion — awareness that writing was possible transmitted via documented Mesopotamian contact (cylinder seals) — without sign-borrowing

holders.name: Orly Goldwasser
holders.work: "Cuneiform and Hieroglyphs in the Bronze Age" (2017)

interpretations.strongest_case: Documented Mesopotamian cylinder-seal imports in Egyptian tombs from Naqada IIb-c (c. 3500-3300 BCE), with a distinctively Egyptian glyptic tradition emerging by Naqada IId (c. 3300 BCE) on a Middle Uruk technological base, establishes real, dated contact in the same window writing emerges.

does_not_demonstrate: That Egyptian hieroglyphic signs were adapted from cuneiform signs (ADAPTATION is excluded by all named scholars)
notes: An older, discredited early-20th-century "Dynastic Race Theory" strand (Flinders Petrie and others) entangled Mesopotamia-priority arguments with racialized claims about a foreign "dynastic race" bringing civilization to Egypt; this has lost mainstream support and should not be conflated with the sober, evidence-based Baines/Regulski/Goldwasser debate that remains live today.
